import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_69/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_69/training_1.csv"

Source3_69_0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
Source3_69_1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_69_0 and Source3_69_1 on "city"
joined_df = pd.merge(Source3_69_0, Source3_69_1, on="city", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by ["Source3_69_0.city", "Source3_69_0.type"], aggregations ["avg(Source3_69_1.fare)"]
# After join, columns from Source3_69_0 and Source3_69_1 are merged, so "city" and "type" come from Source3_69_0,
# and "fare" from Source3_69_1.

# Group by city and type, aggregate average fare
result = (
    joined_df
    .groupby(["city", "type"], as_index=False)
    .agg(fare=("fare", "mean"))
)

# Ensure the schema matches target schema: ['city': string, 'type': string, 'fare': float]
# city and type are already strings, fare is float from aggregation

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_69/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
